minutes.summary: The Select Board ratified a police officer hire, approved a utility pole petition and a conditional one-day alcohol license, and approved a Pride flag raising. The town manager reported on vacancies, fall town meeting items, street lights, and legislation on remote meetings. The board adopted FY23 goals and spent most of the night in a workshop on policies, reaching consensus on term limits and reappointment process changes.

what_happened.line: The Select Board reached consensus of four on term limits: four consecutive terms, then a full-term break, with the policy to go to other boards for input first.
The board agreed to interview incumbents and new applicants together and not to advertise incumbent reappointment bids.
The board approved its FY2023 goals as modified and the town manager's FY2023 goals.
The board approved a conditional one-day alcohol license for Conrad's, tied to proof of insurance and a revised site plan.
The town manager listed possible fall town meeting articles, including assessor inspection funding, a prior-year payroll invoice and a compensation study consultant.

why_it_matters: Term limits and the reappointment process decide how long residents can serve on town boards and how openings are posted, so the draft policy may change who can seek a seat.
The possible fall town meeting articles are spending requests that residents may be asked to vote on.
watch_next: The draft term limit policy, to be circulated to town boards for input before the Select Board finalizes it.
The warrant for the fall special town meeting, which may carry the articles the town manager named.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the main votes (O'Brien appointment, pole petition, Conrad's license, special officers, both sets of goals) and on the key figures (warrants, $54,000 bid, 20-40% road prices, $35,000 inspections). They differ on the Pride flag vote, which only our minutes record as a vote, and on several decisions (H.4991 position, incumbent interviews, talent bank form) that ours describes more firmly than the official minutes do.
